Gentrifying the inner city

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Johannesburgs mayor wants to clean up the inner city, but at what cost?

Summary:
The mayor of Johannesburg has made it clear that he plans on cleaning up the inner city. Old buildings that are being used as housing are being sold and renovated. The occupants are being forcibly removed by the red ants and left with nowhere to go.
The mayor said in a statement that illegal foreigners are leaving JHB with a 300 000 housing deficit and the are the bulk of the people being removed.

Seri, are fighting for the legal right of the occupants. They say that in fact there are 80% SA citizens and 20% foreign nationals occupying all three of the building where they are representing people.

The South African constitution says that housing must be provided for everyone in the country, not just citizens.

We need to unpack both sides of the story: These people are essentially illegally squatting in these buildings, but they are only here because they have nowhere else to go. If we want to 'clean up' the inner city we need to provide alternative accommodation for these people, according to the constitution.

Press Release:


Gentrifying the inner city?
Fattis Mansions once stood as one of the grandest apartment blocks in downtown Johannesburg, but with
broken windows, no electricity and years of neglect, the building is in a severe state of decay. Despite this,
hundreds of people still called it home. Then in July this year, the Red Ants moved in, evicting residents
and dumping all their belongings onto the streets. Developers say they want to return the apartment block
to its former glory, but some residents claim they own the flats they lived in. Gentrifying the inner city, or an
attack on the poor? Carte Blanche investigates.

Script:


Time code CHARACTER / VISUAL
1 00:00 Macfarlane: this tented camp behind me is housing 160 odd homeowners and tenants from a private block of flats in Johannesburg CBD called Fattis Mansion. It is about 6km away form the inner city on a dusty patchy land between 2 rubbish dumps. Ngobeni Funzela a member of the mayoral committee for development planning has been working very closely to try and resolve the inner city housing program at large
2 00:29 MMC and MacFarlane interview Macfarlane: MMC the people that are evicted from fatties mansion they are now living in make shift refugee camps at the moment they do need your help, something needs to be done, there's families, there's children

MMC: that is why we contested in court against this eviction because we at that time believed that we didn’t have enough temporary accommodation for those people to be evicted but unfortunately the court went ahead and issued that eviction and we were left with a crisis.

Macfarlane: there's hardly any sanitation, there hardly and water its women and children that are in a place like that what is being done to help them?

MMC: from what I know is that the disaster management continue to take care of people there although its not sufficient and I totally agree with you that we need to do more.
3 01:09 Voice over The displaced residence of Fattis mansions have already been in this camp for a month and the court is now given the city another 30 days to make alternative arrangement. Edward Pithlane is a home owner at Fattis Mansion in 2000 he was given a government subsidy of about R23 000 as part of the then RDP housing scheme. This together with his own saving meant Edward was able to purchase his flat no 218 at Fattis mansion for R38 000.
4 01:39 Edward I've been living there in Fattis Mansions for 24 years, Me and my child and my wife. The place was very good, nice it was nice that place. That guy takes me out of inner city and throw me here in the camping place so I'm not at all okay here.
5 02:00 Voice over Mary who has asked us to hide her identity was also given a government
Subsidy in the late 90’s and has been living at Fattis with her husband and
Children ever since.
6 02:10 Mary It was my home I stay nicely with my children and my husband and everything we get it at the shops. The shops are down stairs and I’m upstairs. My life is messed up now I cain’t stay with my children and my grand children together as a family like before. I don't know when I say to our government of the thinks is going like this in front of them.
7 02:38 Voice over This is the best solution that the city of Johannesburg can facilitate for these displaced men, women and children. What is going to happen when the mayor begins with his inner city renewal project?

Which will see 80 building in the Johannesburg CBD renovated into low cost housing. A move that will leave 100 displaced and with the current housing deficit of R300 000 and only and out pay of R3500 a year. This seems like a problem that may be bigger than the city can afford to solve.
8 03:10 MMC interview MMC: what will happen is that once we have identified a particular building for it be renovated or for to be developed we are going to make sure that there is an empty building which will be provided by the city that will be able to ready for people to be decanted into them. Just to ensure of course that people are not to be left homeless as we are doing these renovations in the inner city
Mac: so will you also be providing low cost house? At what cost thou?

MMC: So the conditions that we are giving for these developers is be able to cater that gap which is close to R1000 up until R5000

Mac: that might still be too high; these people are paying in the region between R500 and a R1000.

MMC: we say people must be able to be accommodates in back yards they should be able to be accommodation even in areas around the inner city like Rosettenvile
9 04:09 VOICE OVER Although Fattis Mansion is not one of the 80-building ear marked by the inner city renewal project. It is a scary example of the dire situation for the working class working in the inner city. Fattis mansion is a sectional title building consisting of 195 units. FairVest PTYT limited is the registered owner of 10 of the retail sections located on the ground floor in the building. For years Fattis Mansions was ravaged by slums lord and administrators.
In 2010 the electricity was turned of.
In 2014 Fairvest property 2 PTY Limited went to court and requested for Jan Van De Bos to be re instated to be the administrator of the Fattis Mansions body corporate. He was to represent the best interest of all the people living in the building.

To date the building owes the city R11 million
10 05:01 Jan van De Bos interview Jan: the administrator makes all the decisions. The owners are then excluded from any decision making but its obviously mean that the administrator must make decision for the benefit of all the owners and must run it as required by the sectional titles act
11 05:22 Voice over After working as an administrator on the building for 3 years, Jan Van De Bos went to court and request and eviction order sighting that the building was uninhabitable. The building was condemned and the eviction order were given. It went uncontested as the owners and tenants claimed they knew nothing of the eviction until the day the red ants arrived.
12 05:41 Interview with Van De Bos Mac: some of the home owners are saying they never saw eviction notices

Jan: we had to out up eviction notices as many as possible in 5 different places in the building, we had to provide the court with photographs of having the evictions orders there every body knew about the eviction
13 06:03 Voice over The red ants are a private security company hired by the sheriff’s office to execute large eviction. They recall the day they came and violently removed him from his home.
14 06:14 Edward I think there was about 10 trucks of Red Ants then they came in there and jumped off and they attached each and every person there. “ Go out” when you go out also they search you they take ID’s yeah phones from ladies, men’s, I lost everything I haven’t got nothing.
15 06:34 Mac link Mac: subsequently 4 owners and 61 occupants of Fattis Mansion have bought a court application against Jan Van De Bos and Fairvest property PTY Limited opposing the court eviction. They are being represented by the Socio Economic Rights Institute of South Africa.
16 06:52 Ndabe The court needs to ask who are you evicting? Do they stand to be landed homeless as a result of this eviction? Do they have children? Are these uhm women head house holds? Can they afford? Can they afford to live somewhere else? These questions where not asked These questions were no asked therefor this order is incompetent.
17 07:16 Voice over The administrator van de Bos defends his course of action claiming that the building was not fit for human inhabitance
18 07:23 There was nothing operating in the building, no electricity, now water no lifts uhm the refuse had accumulated there. There was no refuse removal so it was impossible for people to live there
19 07:36 Voice over The owners feel that Van De Bos had a hidden agenda as the administrator of the building
20 07:41 Mary Van de Bos caused many problems. They take out the pipe there that for storage just because he wants to win the flat its Van De Bos who stole our flat. Our flat was alright, everything was there water we have water, but when Van De Bos arrived there the water was finished
21 08:00 Interview with van de Bos Mac: when we spoke to some of the owners they said that you allowed for this building can deteriorate so that eviction orders could be enforced upon them.

Jan: I reject that we did what they trying to say that I deliberately brought a building to a situation where eviction was necessary. That’s what they are trying to say I can tell you that its total nonsense

22 08:32 He has an elaborate scheme to take overt the entire building. He has asked a number of our clients who are owners uhm to sell the property to him and if they don't want to sell the property to him what he's going to do is, he's doing to uhm renovate non the less because they are outside and they are not even allowed to come. So he's at this point in time renovating the property, he's destroying it. And whilst we are still in court trying to get ourselves back into the property it’s a specific kind of hijacking
23 09:05 Jan Mac: we've got some of the owner’s right? Some of the owners and these are legal statements that were made in court he “ he also made offers to purchase several units from some of the members after making the situation unbearable for us”.

VDB: I haven't bought any flat that is nonsense. I introduced them to the people and they negotiated a price to sell.

Mac: so you facilitated them selling their property off to specific people that wanted those units okay

24 09:34 Voice overs The renovations that Jan Van Den Bos has committed to undertake on the Communal properties of Fattis Mansion are amounting to around R40 million.
25 09:41 Macfarlane interviews Jan Van De Bos VDB: I have to divide that 40 million between all the owners and all in respect of the size of the unit they have to contribute towards that amount. They were given the opportunity to be bought out. Either they can sell the unit right or take legal action against the owners and recover the money. I was authorized to offer them R10 000 for their unit.

Mac: Do you know hat the values of the properties were?
Bos: uhm look it depends on when they bought uhm but I don't think they paid more than R40 000, R50 000, 60 000 Fairveld paid for the shops at the time R8 million
Mac: what we need to understand the situation of these people that they find themselves right uhm and as you say yes there are no services, there is no electricity but people that’s the only alternative they have at the moment that’s all they have.
VSB: yeah I know but you must also be realistic. You are not being realistic, of course its sad for these people but how did they allow themselves to end up in the place in the first place now they expect somebody else to full them out of this shit
26 11:00 Mac link It is now up to the court to decide what will happen next to Fattis Mansion but for Home owners like Mary and Edward, who already have so little now have even less.
27 11:09 Edward Yeah now this is my home that one I want it back even now
28 11:12 Mary The government cain’t give me the money again, it cain’t give me the house again. That flat I take it as my home.
29 11:22 Macfarlane link And with the budget allocated for the city of Johannesburg housing being half for the 2017/2018 financial year. Mayor Herman Mashaba inner city plan may leave even more homeless.
30 11:36 Ndabe Thousand and thousand of people stand to be displaced in the city of many of these communities in these more than 80 buildings are evicted
